newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn urges Zagreb to rein in Bosnian Croats.
newsitem.headline: Bonn urges Zagreb to rein in Bosnian Croats.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel urged Croatia on Friday to do more to bring to book those responsible for an attack on Moslems in the Bosnian city of Mostar, and to condemn a tirade against the EU by a Bosnian Croat leader.

Kinkel told Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic during talks in Bonn that he was concerned about the situation in Mostar, which remains divided between Moslems and Croats more than a year after the Dayton agreement sealed peace in Bosnia.
The worst confrontation was an incident in which Croats shot dead a Moslem trying to visit a cemetery on the Croat side of the city on February 10, and wounded 21 others.
A United Nations inquiry found that Croat police fired on the Moslems without provocation, but so far the only punishments handed down have been suspended sentences given to three Croat policemen.
Kinkel's ministry said in a statement he had told Granic that "those who are responsible for the attacks...must at last be detained and brought to book".
The statement also said a verbal assault directed at former EU-appointed Mostar administrator Hans Koschnick by Mijo Brajkovic, the rightist former mayor of west Mostar, was unacceptable.
The tirade prompted European Union officials to walk out of a factory inauguration ceremony being attended by Croatian President Franjo Tudjman.

The statement said Kinkel told Granic it was "incomprehensible that something like this should be allowed to happen in the presence of the Croatian President without Croatia formally dissociating itself from it".

Kinkel also urged Granic to use Zagreb's influence on the Bosnian Croats to cooperate in building up the Croat-Moslem federation as set down in the Dayton agreement, to defend human rights, to ensure refugees were allowed to return to their homes and to cooperate with the international tribunal trying to prosecute war criminals.
Germany led the way in recognising Croatia as an independent state and is regarded as its most influential European backer.

Kinkel told Granic Bonn would continue to support Croatia's efforts to join European institutions, but stressed the importance of developing democracy in Croatia and of Zagreb helping to ensure the Dayton agreement was implemented in Bosnia.
